data.title: Accendra Health receives NYSE notice
data.description:
• Accendra Health (ACH)  said on Friday it received a notice from the NYSE after its average closing share price fell below $1 for 30 consecutive trading days.
  • The company plans to notify the NYSE of its intent to cure the deficiency within 10 business days and has six months to regain compliance.
  • Accendra Health is considering options, including a reverse stock split subject to shareholder approval at its next annual meeting, expected in May 2027.
  • The company shares will continue trading on the NYSE during the six-month compliance period, subject to meeting other listing standards.
  • Share -3.43%

data.title: Perrigo may have attracted takeover interest - Betaville
Year-end rally in sight as market breadth starts improving: SA analyst
data.description:
Cestrian Capital Research, investing group leader of Growth Investor Pro, expects this week's market rally across equities (SPY) and bonds (TLT) to persist through the end of the year, despite widespread investor denial and negative sentiment.

Upward market momentum is steadily grinding higher as gains expand beyond mega-cap tech into broader asset classes, the Seeking Alpha analyst noted.

Market breadth strengthened internally, with an increasing share of S&P 500 stocks rising above their 200-day moving averages for the first time in over a month this week.

"The denial is palpable, sentiment is terrible, but equities - and now bonds - are grinding higher.  We expect this to continue into year end."

Wall Street regained some momentum on Friday, after the AI trade came under pressure on Thursday. S&P 500 (SP500) ended the session +0.6%, the Dow (DJI) +0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.6%.

data.title: DuPont, Illinois Tool Works cut to Neutral at J.P. Morgan on downside short-cycle trends
data.description:
DuPont (DD) and Illinois Tool Works (ITW) were downgraded Friday to Neutral from Overweight with $145 and $277 price target, cut from $172 and $300, at J.P. Morgan, which cited concerns over decelerating short-cycle industrial demand into 2027.

"We are in a 'mid-cycle' stage of the industrial cycle - no longer 'early' - as many B2B/industrial end-market up-cycles are quite mature, and the AI up-cycle is entering year 4, [which] coupled with valuations which are not cheap vs. bond yields, caps the degree to which [electrical equipment and multi-industry sector] multiples can re-rate on a relative basis," JPM's Julian Mitchell said in a note.

The analyst said he has a "mildly positive" view of the EE/MI sector with scope for a "catch-up bounce" given the group's recent stock underperformance and likely positive estimate revisionmomentum at Q3 earnings.

JPM said its thesis on DuPont (DD) "primed for a short-cycle recovery with consistent execution" has largely played out, and while seeing improving trends for some pockets of the company's portfolio, "overall we see organic growth deceleration" into 2027 following above company average organic growth in 2026.

On Illinois Tool Works (ITW), Mitchell said he does "not view the overall short-cycle industrial complex particularly favorably, as we think manufacturing PMIs may not show much further improvement from current levels," meaning little opportunity for positive estimate revision at the company and a fair current valuation for the stock.

Additionally, JPM started Trane (TT) Trane at Overweight as "a best-in-class HVAC name, and we expect it to continue to thrive relative to the group and other HVAC pure-play names," and Carrier Global (CARR) at Neutral as "valuation looks somewhat cheap, but there is considerable uncertainty over the earnings outlook."

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway advances for seven consecutive sessions
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) shares clocked seven straight sessions of gains, as the stock was up 0.9% at $515.45 on Friday.

The holding company gained over 2% in the preceding six sessions. 

Recently, Berkshire Hathaway purchased $53.9M of Lennar (LEN) shares in the last three days of September, pushing the insurance conglomerate's ownership to a stake valued at ~$2.16B. 

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, BRK has a Hold rating with a score of 3.48 out of 5. The company received A+ in the prospect of profitability, while it received D+ in growth factor.

Seeking Alpha analysts are positive and see the stock as a Buy.

"BRK.B's traditional passive allocation strategy is increasingly at risk, with real returns on T-bills eroded by inflation and limited acquisition targets that meet strict criteria. Strategic pivot toward large-scale energy infrastructure—especially nuclear and geothermal—could unlock long-term value, leveraging Berkshire’s unique capital structure and operating assets," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis report.

data.title: Costco closes nearly flat despite September sales growth
data.description:
Costco Wholesale (COST) closed almost flat on Friday, edging down 0.1% to $945.01.

The stock gained 4.13% over the previous six sessions, outperforming the S&P 500’s 1.48% advance. Year to date, however, Costco shares have risen 9.63%, trailing the index’s 13.44% gain.

The muted performance came despite strong September sales. Costco reported net sales of $30.0B, up 13% year over year, while comparable sales rose 11.4% and e-commerce comparable sales climbed 19%.

 However, a later Labor Day  calendar in the U.S. and Canada boosted September total and comparable sales growth by slightly more than 50 basis points. Shares have remained below the $1,000 mark since May 28.

Despite the company’s strong operating performance, Seeking Alpha analyst Dividend Collection Agency maintained a Sell rating, citing Costco’s elevated valuation. Although Q4 sales rose 11.2% and EPS increased 15%, growth in membership income and traffic is slowing. Trading at more than 40x forward earnings, the stock may need to decline 15%-20% to offer an attractive entry point, even with its strong balance sheet and robust free cash flow.

Seeking Alpha’s Quant Rating also reflects valuation concerns, assigning Costco a Hold rating with a score of 3.31 out of 5. The company earns an A+ for profitability, a C+ for growth, and an F- for Valuation.

Wall Street analysts remain more positive, with 24 rating the stock Buy or higher and 13 assigning a Hold rating. Seeking Alpha analysts are more cautious, with a consensus Hold rating.

data.title: Stocks close in green as tech selloff eases
data.description:
Wall Street regained some momentum on Friday, after the AI trade came under pressure on Thursday.

S&P 500 (SP500) +0.6%, the Dow (DJI) +0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.6%. 

Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors were in the green, led by real estate and consumer discretionary as the top gainers, while communication services was the biggest loser.

Tech shares came under pressure on Thursday amid revenue concerns surrounding OpenAI (OPENAI). Reports indicated that OpenAI's annualized revenue reached $50B at the end of September, below the $68B figure reported the previous month.

"This week the rally broadened out," noted Cestrian Capital Research, investing group leader of Growth Investor Pro. "The S&P500 and Nasdaq-100 continued to advance but for the first time  since mid-August, the Dow Jones was green on the week. As were U.S. government bonds. As was gold. Further, the share of S&P500 stocks over their 200-day moving averages also increased during the week- also for the first time since mid August. The denial is palpable, sentiment is terrible, but equities - and now bonds - are grinding higher. We expect this to continue into year end."

On the economic front, consumer sentiment fell more than expected in October's initial reading as inflation expectations accelerated.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 4 basis points to 4.80%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 1 basis point to 5.25%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) slipped 1 basis point to 5.60%.

data.title: Delta expects $5.10-$5.60 EPS and ~$2.5B free cash flow for 2026 amid projected $4.25 fuel
ArcelorMittal raised to Buy at UBS on upbeat European steel price outlook
data.description:
ArcelorMittal (MT) jumped 4.6% in Friday's trading as UBS upgraded the steel producer to Buy from Neutral with a €71 price target, raised from €61, as the bank said it expects a large rally in European Union steel prices in the next six months and noted shares have shed nearly 20% of their value during the past month, leaving the stock oversold and sensitive to any positive catalyst.

ArcelorMittal (MT) shares are fairly valued at ~€750/ton spot hot-rolled coil, but free cash flow yields rise to 6%-8% at €820-€850/ton HRC despite substantial growth capital expenditures, UBS analyst Andrew Jones calculated, saying every €10/ton increase in the European price adds ~$325M to the company's EBITDA and ~$250M to free cash flow.

Adding to the constructive tone, ArcelorMittal (MT) Eisenhüttenstadt resumed operations at its blast furnace this week, signaling a gradual normalization of European production capacity after a period of curtailments and disruptions, the analyst said.

While noting risks to North American HRC pricing and import risk in Brazil and India, Jones said ArcelorMittal (MT) is gaining most of the market share from import displacement and is the most liquid play on the European growth theme.

data.title: ICON upgraded at BofA on better CRO demand, improved 2027 visibility
data.description:
• BofA Securities upgraded ICON Public Limited Co. (ICLR) to neutral from underweight as it sees improved demand for contract research organization services as Street estimates for the top 50 biopharma companies see R&D spending growth of ~4% in 2027.
  • The bank also raised its price target to $185 from $160 (~12% upside based on Oct. 8 close).
  • "CRO demand has improved, with resilient large pharma spending and better RFP activity, proposal quality and biotech win rates," noted analyst Michael Ryskin.
  • However, he added that pass-through—external costs borne by ICON that are eventually reimbursed by the sponsor—"remains elevated given the mix of recent awards and could remain at "higher levels into 2027, constraining margin expansion even as revenue growth recovers."
